... RUN CHASE ...

The second break was more bitter for Zimbabwe as they kept on losing wickets in a flurry. Wanindu Hasaranga again was in action and the magician eventually ended up with 7 wickets. Yes, seven. In a crucial match, Zimbabwe fell miserably to just one man. Now they have a big task ahead. Zimbabwe, to draw the series have to do something magical which looks very hard at the moment. Sri Lanka on the other hand will be eager to chase it down. Stay tuned.

It was basically Wanindu Hasaranga vs Zimbabwe today with rain showers in between to sum up the innings. The Zimbabwe openers gave a really good start with both timing the ball really well but just went it was going well for Zimbabwe, the rain came down which hampered their game-flow. After that it was all about Wanindu Hasaranga who ran through the top three before again the rain gods decided to show up.

Commentary.Commentary: The Zimbabwe openers, Joylord Gumbie and Takudzwanashe Kaitano are out in the middle. Dilshan Madushanka to begin. Here we go...

A couple of changes for both the sides but the most eye-catrching one is the inclusion of Wanindu Hasaranga! He is back for Lanka after quite some time. Have to feel a little sorry for Jeffrey Vandersay, after all he did in the last game, he has been benched but that was always going to be the case once Wanindu Hasaranga was fit. Also, it is a debut for Shevon Daniel. For Zimbabwe, Wellington Masakadza and Luke Jongwe come in.

Zimbabwe (PLAYING XI) - Joylord Gumbie (WK), Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Craig Ervine (C), Milton Shumba, Sikandar Raza, Ryan Burl, Clive Madande, Wellington Masakadza, Luke Jongwe, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani.

Sri Lanka (PLAYING XI) - Avishka Fernando, Kusal Mendis (WK/C), Shevon Daniel, Sadeera Samarawickrama, Janith Liyanage, Charith Asalanka, Sahan Arachchige, Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, Dushmantha Chameera, Dilshan Madushanka.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and ELECTED TO BAT!

It was the likes of Dushmantha Chameera and Jeffrey Vandersay who held their nerve to give Sri Lanka a narrow win in the second ODI. The hosts now have an unassailable lead heading into the third game as the first game was abandoned due to rain. Anything other than a loss will see them take the series. For Zimbabwe this is a must-win, despite the loss in the last game, they will head into this one with confidence. They showed immense character defending a total which we thought would have been chased quite easily. They would hope to get over the line this time and level the series one each. Let us hope we are in for another exciting encounter. Toss and teams in a bit.
